message.content:
Keysight Technologies Inc reported record results for the quarter ended 2026-07-31, with revenue of $1.85 billion, net income of $397 million, earnings per share of $2.82, a gross margin of 65.87% and a net margin of 21.51% [D1]. Revenue grew 36.54% and net income grew 107.85% from a year earlier, and earnings per share grew 63.95% to $2.82 against an estimate of $2.16 [D1]. Revenue in the Communications Solutions Group was $1,345 million, up 43.09%, and revenue in the Electronic Industrial Solutions Group was $501 million, up 21.6% [D1]. Sequential revenue growth was 7.51% [D1].

Management guided the fourth quarter to revenue of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion and earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40 on a diluted share count of approximately 172 million, with the midpoint of the revenue range representing growth of approximately 37% [D1]. The market's argument is less about the size of the quarter just reported than about what limits the next one, because management said demand is far exceeding its ability to supply and that the supply chain will remain the governor of near-term revenue [D3]. Management also said the supply situation is likely to be nonlinear and that the supply environment is less flexible than a year earlier [D3]. A related argument concerns the quality of profitability, since management cautioned that one-time tariff impacts in fiscal 2026 will not repeat [D3].

The bullish case rests on the demand signal, with management expecting fourth-quarter orders slightly above the third quarter and the sales organization confident of another record quarter [D3]. The bearish case rests on the same point, because analysts pressed management on whether the guidance is capped by supply rather than by demand [D3]. Covering analysts remain constructive, with strong agreement that earnings estimates should rise [D5]. The debate therefore turns on whether supply rather than demand is the binding constraint for the next several quarters [D3].

The plan is to hold the position into the fourth quarter and to judge the company against the guided revenue range of $1.93 billion to $1.95 billion and guided earnings per share of $3.34 to $3.40 [D1]. The first checkpoint is gross margin, where a print at or above the latest quarter's 65.87% would show that margin is holding without the one-time tariff benefit [D1]. The second is net margin, where a print at or above 21.51% would do the same [D1]. The third is supply, since management named the supply chain as the governor of near-term revenue for the next several quarters [D3]. A fourth-quarter revenue print inside the guided range with margins at or above the latest quarter's levels would confirm the thesis [D1]. Revenue below the low end of $1.93 billion would instead confirm that supply is the binding constraint [D3].
